title: Qi
capsule: The state of Qi (齊) was a major Zhou fief occupying the Shandong Peninsula and adjacent plains, traditionally founded by Jiang Ziya (Lü Shang) as reward for his role in the Zhou conquest of Shang c. 1045 BCE. Qi rose to interstate dominance under Duke Huan (r. 685–643 BCE), the first recognised hegemon (bà), guided by minister Guan Zhong whose fiscal and administrative reforms transformed Qi into an economic powerhouse through salt and iron monopolies. The original Jiang ruling house was displaced by the Tian clan, which obtained Zhou recognition as legitimate rulers in 386 BCE; the new Tian Qi survived into the Warring States era but was eliminated by a combined Yan-led invasion in 284 BCE that briefly overran nearly the entire state, and a much-diminished Qi finally succumbed to Qin conquest in 221 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extent is reasonably reconstructed from Shiji and Zhanguoce, but precise annual boundaries during the Warring States period involve scholarly interpolation.
